ashok: heads up — us-west fabric glitch reduced inter-rack throughput ~40% an hour ago, we're seeing queue growth on inference pools. suggestion: flip admit control to a 'soft-admit' degrade mode instead of hard rejects so short requests can still complete.

maria: can you paste the crit metrics? p95/p99, queue length and drop rate?

ashok: p95 token latency +12%, p99 +40%. queued requests up from ~120 to 820, drop rate spiked to 18% on the fastestpath. GPU util still ~85 but network egress across racks is the choke. logs: `conn-errors: 412, retransmits: 1500`

liam: +1 for soft-admit. If we queue too long we hold KV caches and starve new short requests. prefer degrade that prioritizes <512 token jobs and short prompt + few-shot.

olivia: propose policy: short_request_priority = true, max_queue_ms = 400, degrade_fraction = 0.45 for best-effort tier. That gives room and avoids full rejects. also add fallback to cheaper quantized variant for long jobs.

ashok: drafted a minimal policy snippet — can we review quickly?

ashok: ```yaml
admit_policy:
  mode: soft_admit
  max_queue_ms: 400
  short_request_threshold_tokens: 512
  short_priority_only: true
  degrade_fraction: 0.45
  fallback_model: llama-3-small-quant
  backoff_hint_ms: 100
```

maria: this looks reasonable. question: what's rollout plan and abort criteria? we need clear SLO triggers.

liam: rollout: canary 5% us-west cluster -> monitor 10m -> 25% -> 100% if p99 latency improvement or stable. abort if errors increase >1.5x or drop rate >5% persistently. add regression alert on token-per-second and cost-per-token (>10% increase).

olivia: add a metric check for KV-cache pressure (rv: kv_cache_miss_rate) and GPU-cycle fragmentation. if cache miss >3% during canary, rollback.

ashok: cost note: spinning burst nodes in another region to bypass fabric would add ~6k GPU-hours and >$10k/day in cross-region egress. prefer soft-admit + fallback models first.

sre-oncall: using degrade keeps user-facing error rate lower, good for incidents. make sure runbook includes `rctl admit rollback` steps and that oncall can flip to hard-reject quickly if queue memory pressure rises.

ashok: agreed. runbook snippet: `rctl apply admit-policy us-west soft-admit.yaml` then `rctl monitor admit-metrics --watch`. rollback: `rctl apply admit-policy us-west hard-reject.yaml`

deploy-bot: starting canary rollout: us-west-zone-a 5% at 1728130200 :rocket:

maria: monitoring dashboards set: p99_latency, queue_length, drop_rate, kv_cache_miss_rate, errors. alert thresholds added. :eyes:

liam: if canary passes at +25% we should also enable model fallback auto-switch for long jobs (threshold: queue_ms > 300 -> route to quant variant).

olivia: note for docs: update inference-runbook/admit-policies.md with new soft-admit pattern and example configs + regression watchlist.

ashok: thanks everyone — will watch the canary and post updates. next check in 15m.

sre-oncall: oncall acked, will take alerts.

deploy-bot: canary reached 25% at 1728132000, metrics stable so far.

maria: initial 30m check: p99 down from +40% to +18%, drop rate from 18% -> 3%. keeping a close eye on KV cache pressure.

ashok: good. continuing rollout to 100% unless any triggers fire. will keep notes for postmortem including network root cause and whether this policy should be default for network partial outages.

olivia: follow-up item: run load-test simulating 40% inter-rack bandwidth loss to validate degrade heuristics. putting on eng-infra backlog.
